first_playback_tags.protocol: Use unchanged Reel PlaybackSounds(AST) and EventHistory(YAMNet) on exactly the same first four seconds. A hit means the human leaf label appears in the union of returned names. Other cues, captions, and GPT reasoning are excluded from this comparison. Multiple names may be reported per clip.

isolated_sources.prompt: What made the most distinctive sound in this recording? Name the single most specific sound source you can support, in a few English words. If you can describe its character but cannot identify the source, answer "unknown". Give only JSON {"source":"..."}.
isolated_sources.selection: From the 244 held-out recordings, take distinct leaf classes, 16 with references and 6 without. Sort by SHA256(local-gpt-first-source/ID), use durations 1.45 to 7.5s, shuffle by SHA256(shuffleID). No target names in filenames, inputs or prompts.
isolated_sources.protocol: One first view, original full recording up to 7.5s. Identical images, local speech, caption, AST and YAMNet outputs. Compare without vs with recorded-example evidence from released samples. The answerer received visualized evidence on anonymous image-and-text MCP playback with no native WAV. The optional 30B waveform helper was disabled in both arms. New signed-in gpt-6.1-terra session for each answer with shell and plugins disabled. One run per arm. Identical-input replies may differ.
isolated_sources.rubric: Compare the answer with the human source label, taking accepted synonyms, paraphrases, or equivalent sound actions as exact. "unknown" is unknown. If the answer names only a parent or a plausible subtype of the labeled source for which the extra specificity cannot be verified, record compatible. Record wrong for a distinct incompatible physical source/action. Extra details around a correct source may be unverified without invalidating recognition of that source. Judge each pair once, unaware of arm. Evaluate the class label, not other sounds that might be present.
isolated_sources.grading: A separate fresh local gpt-6.1-terra session graded unique lowercase label-answer pairs in hash-shuffled order, without arm information. No manual overrides.

moving_films.attribution: AVCaps, Sudarsanam, Martín Morató, Hakala and Virtanen. CC BY-NC 4.0 research release.
moving_films.selection: Eight cached films not present in earlier published Reel reports, ordered by SHA256(reference-source-av-frozen/+ID). Required a human audio panel and full duration between 1.5 and 22 seconds. At least three sound-only reference captions per film.
moving_films.protocol: Three sequential views per anonymous film through a staged MCP server under the same signed-in GPT model as the isolated sound panel. Free picture-and-sound impression then separate sound and picture recall. Exact same released images and existing reports in both arms, with example matches added only after. No native WAV or 30B question reader. Compare each heard response with the human audio-only captions using the existing first-impression scorer. Wide uncertainty with eight films.

door.protocol: Same closed door up to --until 8.5 seconds in two MCP turns. A has the metal jingle, B retains the background, C has the same prefix as A with a different future. Compare the released text and every attached picture by SHA-256. Exact listen past 8.5 rejected; all checks completed. Silence replaces every sound sample. Picture-only omits the audio track.
door.prompt: Describe what you heard before playback stopped. If you heard a distinct brief sound, describe its character and name a source only if you can identify it. Give any intelligible words only if the recording supports them. Answer in a single English sentence.

responses.A: A brief series of light metallic jingles and rattles breaks the quiet, with no intelligible speech.
responses.B: A faint, steady fan-like hiss continues until playback stops, with no intelligible speech.
responses.silent: There was silence throughout, with no audible sounds or speech.
responses.picture: I can’t determine what was heard because no audio was provided.

local_cost.protocol: Apple M4 Pro, hosted helper only, original mono clips in the isolated panel order capped at the first four seconds. One resident process, one request per clip. Cold refers to a new process with cached weights. Peak RSS is the summed resident set of the benchmark process and descendants, not an estimate of hardware minimum or additional memory per video.
